title: Best Carbon Monoxide Alarms UK
short: Five carbon monoxide alarms tested with an aerosol trigger spray in a sealed bag to check response speed, from a £17 basic alarm to a £90 smart alarm.
intro: A carbon monoxide alarm is one of the few home safety products where a slow reaction can be life-threatening, and Expert Reviews warns that not every model is equally sensitive or reliable. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup (published 14 May 2024, not updated since), where testers sprayed a specific aerosol test spray for up to three seconds into a transparent plastic bag containing each alarm and did not recommend any that failed to respond promptly. They also assessed controls, displays, any Wi-Fi or app features, and how easy each alarm was to fit. Expert Reviews' original top pick, Google's Nest Protect, has since been discontinued, so we have left it out (see the buying guide below).

products.name: 7DCOC
products.badge: Recommended, best for camping and travel
products.best_for: Buyers who want a low-cost alarm that shows CO readings, and one certified for caravans, boats and camping
products.key_spec: 10-year lifespan, 3x AA batteries (replace roughly every 2 years), LCD showing CO readings from 10ppm, certified for camping, caravanning, travel and boats
products.summary: Expert Reviews singled this one out for its sensitive sensor, which takes a CO reading every 15 seconds, and a small LCD that displays readings once they reach 10ppm. It sounds its 85dB alarm if CO stays at 41ppm or above for 60 minutes, and it is BS EN 50291-2 certified for camping, caravanning, travel and even use on a boat. The tester had no issues in testing. The catch is that its three AA batteries need replacing roughly every two years, which Expert Reviews says means it won't comply with the new Scottish regulations.
pros: Sensitive sensor that takes a reading every 15 seconds
LCD shows actual CO readings, not just an alert
Certified for camping, caravanning, travel and boats
Affordable
cons: Batteries need replacing roughly every 2 years
Won't comply with the new Scottish regulations, per Expert Reviews

products.name: SC-08
products.badge: Best combination smoke and CO alarm
products.best_for: Buyers who want one unit covering both smoke and CO, for a room with a gas fire, stove, fireplace or boiler
products.key_spec: Smoke and CO in one unit, 10-year lifespan, sealed-in lithium battery, 3cm LCD, 85dB alarm
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this earns its keep by combining a photoelectric smoke sensor and an electrochemical CO sensor in one unit, with an 85dB siren the tester called unlikely to be slept through. It was quick to respond to the CO test spray, and a 3cm LCD shows a real-time CO reading once levels pass 30 parts per million, along with battery level. The battery is sealed in and non-replaceable, promising 10 years of continuous protection.
pros: Smoke and carbon monoxide detection in one unit
Quick to respond to the CO test spray
No battery changes for 10 years
Loud 85dB alarm
cons: Battery is sealed in and can't be replaced

products.name: Pro Connected FP1820-W2-R
products.best_for: Larger homes wanting every alarm to sound together
products.key_spec: 10-year lifespan, built-in lithium battery, Wi-Safe2 mesh, up to 50 devices on one network, 85dB alarm
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this forms part of FireAngel's Pro Connected range of smoke, CO and heat detectors, which interconnect so that when one unit detects a problem, every installed unit sounds its 85dB alarm at once. It also sends app notifications saying which unit triggered. The tester found the setup fiddly, using the supplied Ethernet-connected wireless gateway box, but every alarm sounded when tested. The CO alarm also works as a standalone detector if bought on its own.
pros: Every interconnected alarm sounds together
App alerts say which unit was triggered
Works standalone if bought on its own
Loud 85dB alarms
cons: Fiddly setup using the supplied gateway box

products.name: Smart CO Alarm
products.badge: Best smart and simple CO alarm
products.best_for: Buyers who want smart monitoring without needing a separate hub
products.key_spec: 10-year lifespan, built-in lithium battery, app shows live CO level, 85dB alarm
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this surprisingly easy to set up: push and twist it onto its wall mount, install the Netatmo Security app, pick your Wi-Fi and tell the app which room it's in, with no complex hub involved. It was sensitive and reliable in testing, setting off within seconds, and the app shows the current CO level and lets you check the alarm is online and working. The catch is the price for a stand-alone alarm.

pros: Easy setup, no separate hub required
Set off within seconds in testing
App shows the current CO level and confirms the alarm is online
Loud 85dB alarm

products.name: Lifesaver 5CO
products.best_for: Buyers who want a straightforward, affordable alarm with no smart features
products.key_spec: 10-year lifespan, AA batteries (replace roughly every 3 years), LED indicators, 85dB alarm
products.summary: Expert Reviews describes this as a wallet-friendly Kidde that now has an upgraded ten-year lifespan. It's not quite as sensitive as the Kidde 7DCOC but was only a couple of seconds behind in raising the alarm in testing, sounding after 60-90 minutes of exposure to 50ppm or above. It's simple to use, with clear red and green LED indicators and a very noisy warning when its batteries fail or the sensor reaches end of life. The downside is that the batteries need swapping roughly every three years, and Expert Reviews says it isn't suitable for Scottish homes, though it is suitable for a boat or caravan.

guide.q: How does the aerosol test actually work?
guide.a: Expert Reviews sprayed a specific aerosol test spray for up to three seconds into a sealed transparent bag containing each alarm. Their rule is that an alarm which doesn't respond promptly isn't recommended, so every alarm here passed. The Netatmo set off within seconds, and the Kidde Lifesaver 5CO was only a couple of seconds behind the more sensitive Kidde 7DCOC.

guide.q: Does pressing the test button prove my alarm works?
guide.a: Not fully. Expert Reviews points out that the test button doesn't actually test the sensor, it only checks that the circuit is working. That's why an alarm's end-of-life and battery warnings matter, and why it's worth replacing an alarm on schedule.

guide.q: How long do these alarms actually last?
guide.a: All five here claim a 10-year life, but Expert Reviews notes that CO sensors typically last between five and seven years and only a few manufacturers claim ten. Its advice is to play it safe and replace an alarm a year or two before its life is supposed to run out, and it cites US tests showing alarms over eight years old can fail to detect CO at levels above 400ppm.

guide.q: Can I use these in Scotland?
guide.a: Check before you buy. Expert Reviews says both Kidde models, the 7DCOC and the Lifesaver 5CO, won't comply with the new Scottish regulations because they run on batteries that need replacing. The X-Sense, FireAngel and Netatmo alarms have built-in or sealed batteries instead. We haven't checked them against the Scottish rules ourselves, so confirm the current requirements for your home.

guide.q: What happened to the Nest Protect?
guide.a: Expert Reviews' original top pick, Google's Nest Protect smart smoke and CO alarm, has been discontinued. Tom's Guide reported on 28 March 2025 that Google was ending sales, selling remaining stock until supplies run out and supporting existing units until they expire. Google's announced replacement, a First Alert alarm, was announced for the US and Canada. Because these alarms have a fixed life from the day they're made, a unit from old stock has less life left, so we've left it out. For a smart alarm, see the Netatmo above.

guide.q: Do I need a smart, app-connected alarm?
guide.a: A smart alarm like the Netatmo sends notifications to your phone even when you're not home, useful for a holiday home or checking on a relative remotely. The FireAngel interconnects with other FireAngel alarms so they all sound together. A basic alarm like the Kidde Lifesaver 5CO is much cheaper and just as capable of sounding a loud local alarm, which is all that's needed if someone is always home to hear it.

guide.q: Combined smoke and CO alarm, or separate units?
guide.a: A combined alarm like the X-Sense SC-08 saves fitting two devices and gives you one thing to maintain. Expert Reviews suggests mounting a CO alarm in the kitchen or next to a fireplace or boiler, and most manufacturers suggest siting it near a gas appliance. See our [smoke alarms](/smoke-alarms/) guide if you'd rather buy dedicated smoke detectors separately.
